sentences.text: Atlantosuchus was an extinct crocodylomorph found in Morocco, distinguished by having the most elongate snout relative to body size of any dyrosaurid.
The genus was described by Buffetaut and Wouters in 1979, with the type species identified as A. coupatezi in the same publication.
Scientists believe Rhabdognathus is the closest relative of Atlantosuchus, a relationship supported by current phylogenetic analysis.
Atlantosuchus belongs to the family Dyrosauridae and is part of the parent group Hyposaurinae.

Its broader classification places it within the unranked family Mesoeucrocodylia, the superorder Crocodylomorpha, the infraclass Archosauromorpha, the subclass Diapsida, the class Sauropsida, the kingdom Animalia, and the phylum Chordata.
Consequently, Atlantosuchus is classified as a reptile.
This animal lived during the Late Palaeocene epoch, specifically from 66 to 61.66 million years ago within the Danian stage.
